questions.q: For whom does the singer want to sing?
questions.a: The singer wants to sing for his beloved.

questions.q: What is the song of the singer about?
questions.a: The song is about the vineyard of his beloved.

questions.q: What did he do to the vineyard?
questions.a: He dug it up, cleared it of stones, planted it with a choice vine, and built a tower and a winepress in it.

questions.q: What did the vineyard bring forth?
questions.a: The vineyard brought forth wild grapes.

questions.q: What are the inhabitants of Jerusalem and the men of Judah to judge?
questions.a: They are to judge between the beloved and his vineyard.

questions.q: What happened even though the vineyard’s owner had done everything he could for it?
questions.a: It still produced only wild grapes.

questions.q: What will the beloved do to his vineyard?
questions.a: He will remove the hedge so it can be trampled and burned, break down the wall, stop pruning and hoeing it, and keep rain from falling on it.

questions.q: Who is the vineyard of Yahweh of Armies?
questions.a: Yahweh’s vineyard is the house of Israel.

questions.q: What did Yahweh wait for?
questions.a: Yahweh waited for justice and righteousness.

questions.q: What did Yahweh get instead of justice and righteousness?
questions.a: Yahweh got bloodshed instead of justice, and a cry for help instead of righteousness.

questions.q: What do the people in verse 8 do to houses and fields?
questions.a: They join house to house and field to field until there is no room left for others, and they live alone in the land.

questions.q: What will happen to many houses?
questions.a: Many large, beautiful houses will be empty, with no one living in them.

questions.q: What will happen to the harvest from large vineyards and fields?
questions.a: The harvest will be very small compared to what was planted.

questions.q: What do the people in verse 11 do from morning until night?
questions.a: They drink beer in the morning and wine late into the night until they are drunk.

questions.q: What do the people ignore while they feast with music and wine?
questions.a: They ignore what Yahweh is doing.

questions.q: Why will the people of Israel go into exile?
questions.a: They will go into exile because they do not know Yahweh.

questions.q: Who will go down into Sheol, the place of the dead?
questions.a: Both the leaders and the common people, along with those who loved to celebrate, will go down into it.

questions.q: What will happen to proud people?
questions.a: They will be humbled.

questions.q: What exalts Yahweh of Armies?
questions.a: Yahweh’s justice exalts him.

questions.q: How is the Holy God recognized as holy?
questions.a: He is recognized as holy because he does what is right.

questions.q: What will lambs and other animals do on the land that has become desolate?
questions.a: They will graze there as usual.

questions.q: What are the people in verse 18 compared to as they hold onto their sin?
questions.a: They are like people pulling a heavy cart of sin with ropes made of lies.

questions.q: What do these people say about the Holy One of Israel’s plan?
questions.a: They say that he should hurry and bring it about quickly so they can see it.

questions.q: What do the people in verse 20 say about good and evil?
questions.a: They say that evil actions are good and that good actions are evil.

questions.q: How do the people in verse 21 view themselves?
questions.a: They view themselves as wise and clever.

questions.q: What are the people in verse 22 skilled at doing?
questions.a: They are skilled at drinking wine and mixing beer to make it stronger.

questions.q: What do these people do in exchange for a bribe?
questions.a: They declare guilty people innocent and punish innocent people instead.

questions.q: Why will Israel’s root rot, and their blossom blow away like dust?
questions.a: Israel’s root will rot, and their blossom will blow away like dust because they have rejected the law of Yahweh and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

questions.q: What does Yahweh do because he is angry with his people?
questions.a: He uses his power to punish them so severely that the mountains shake and dead bodies lie in the streets.

questions.q: How will Yahweh call a far away nation to come?
questions.a: He will call them by raising a banner and whistling for them.

questions.q: How will that far away nation come?
questions.a: That far away nation will come speedily and promptly.

questions.q: What is true about the soldiers in this attacking army?
questions.a: None of them grows weary or stumbles, and none of them slumbers or sleeps.

questions.q: What are the horses’ hooves and the chariot wheels compared to?
questions.a: The horses’ hooves are compared to flint, and the chariot wheels are compared to a whirlwind.

questions.q: What does the army do after it growls like a lion?
questions.a: It seizes the prey and carries it away, and no one can rescue it.

questions.q: What will a person see when they look at the land on that day?
questions.a: They will see darkness and trouble, and the light will be darkened by clouds.

commentary.text: The state and conduct of the Jewish nation. (Is. 5:1-7) The judgments which would come. (Is. 5:8-23) The executioners of these judgments. (Is. 5:24-30)

Is. 5:1-7 Christ is God's beloved Son, and our beloved Saviour. The care of the Lord over the church of Israel, is described by the management of a vineyard. The advantages of our situation will be brought into the account another day. He planted it with the choicest vines; gave them a most excellent law, instituted proper ordinances. The temple was a tower, where God gave tokens of his presence. He set up his altar, to which the sacrifices should be brought; all the means of grace are denoted thereby. God expects fruit from those that enjoy privileges. Good purposes and good beginnings are good things, but not enough; there must be vineyard fruit; thoughts and affections, words and actions, agreeable to the Spirit. It brought forth bad fruit. Wild grapes are the fruits of the corrupt nature. Where grace does not work, corruption will. But the wickedness of those that profess religion, and enjoy the means of grace, must be upon the sinners themselves. They shall no longer be a peculiar people. When errors and vice go without check or control, the vineyard is unpruned; then it will soon be grown over with thorns. This is often shown in the departure of God's Spirit from those who have long striven against him, and the removal of his gospel from places which have long been a reproach to it. The explanation is given. It is sad with a soul, when, instead of the grapes of humility, meekness, love, patience, and contempt of the world, for which God looks, there are the wild grapes of pride, passion, discontent, and malice, and contempt of God; instead of the grapes of praying and praising, the wild grapes of cursing and swearing. Let us bring forth fruit with patience, that in the end we may obtain everlasting life.

Is. 5:8-23 Here is a woe to those who set their hearts on the wealth of the world. Not that it is sinful for those who have a house and a field to purchase another; but the fault is, that they never know when they have enough. Covetousness is idolatry; and while many envy the prosperous, wretched man, the Lord denounces awful woes upon him. How applicable to many among us! God has many ways to empty the most populous cities. Those who set their hearts upon the world, will justly be disappointed. Here is woe to those who dote upon the pleasures and the delights of sense. The use of music is lawful; but when it draws away the heart from God, then it becomes a sin to us. God's judgments have seized them, but they will not disturb themselves in their pleasures. The judgments are declared. Let a man be ever so high, death will bring him low; ever so mean, death will bring him lower. The fruit of these judgments shall be, that God will be glorified as a God of power. Also, as a God that is holy; he shall be owned and declared to be so, in the righteous punishment of proud men. Those are in a woful condition who set up sin, and who exert themselves to gratify their base lusts. They are daring in sin, and walk after their own lusts; it is in scorn that they call God the Holy One of Israel. They confound and overthrow distinctions between good and evil. They prefer their own reasonings to Divine revelations; their own devices to the counsels and commands of God. They deem it prudent and politic to continue profitable sins, and to neglect self-denying duties. Also, how light soever men make of drunkenness, it is a sin which lays open to the wrath and curse of God. Their judges perverted justice. Every sin needs some other to conceal it.

Is. 5:24-30 Let not any expect to live easily who live wickedly. Sin weakens the strength, the root of a people; it defaces the beauty, the blossoms of a people. When God's word is despised, and his law cast away, what can men expect but that God should utterly abandon them? When God comes forth in wrath, the hills tremble, fear seizes even great men. When God designs the ruin of a provoking people, he can find instruments to be employed in it, as he sent for the Chaldeans, and afterwards the Romans, to destroy the Jews. Those who would not hear the voice of God speaking by his prophets, shall hear the voice of their enemies roaring against them. Let the distressed look which way they will, all appears dismal. If God frowns upon us, how can any creature smile? Let us diligently seek the well-grounded assurance, that when all earthly helps and comforts shall fail, God himself will be the strength of our hearts, and our portion for ever.
